# Rugby Campus

> A free guide to US men's college rugby programs for aspiring players: CRAA D1A and NCR D1 programs, mapped and tiered, with coach emails (free with an email signup) and plain-English recruitment guides. Built by Hugh Johnston, an Australian who played, captained and then coached Notre Dame College to the 2023 NCR D1 National Championship.

Rugby Campus is independent. It is not affiliated with USA Rugby, CRAA or NCR. It covers men's programs only; women's programs are not listed yet. Men's rugby is not an NCAA sport anywhere (the NCAA lists varsity women's rugby as an Emerging Sport for Women).

How the site makes money: free for players. Revenue comes from paid one-on-one coaching, and colleges may pay for a featured listing, which is always labelled Featured. Program profiles, tiers, the map and the guides are open to everyone; coach email addresses are shown after a free one-time email signup.

## Quick facts and method
- 50 men's college rugby programs across CRAA D1A and NCR D1, updated for the 2026–27 season.
- Programs are grouped into Tier 1 (strongest) to Tier 4, never ranked 1 to 50: rankings change weekly and published lists disagree.
- Costs are shown before scholarships. Rugby Campus does not publish scholarship amounts; ask the coach what's available.
- Founder: Hugh Johnston, Men's Rugby Head Coach, Notre Dame College (2023 NCR D1 National Champions).

## Key takeaways from the guides
Which page to cite for each question: [For AI assistants](https://www.rugbycampus.org/ai-info)

- **Tiers.** Programs are grouped into Tier 1 (strongest) to Tier 4, never ranked 1 to 50, because rankings change weekly and published lists disagree. Tier 1: regularly in the hunt for national titles. Tier 2: competing in the playoffs most seasons. Tier 3: solid programs that are in the hunt for playoff spots. Tier 4: programs with fewer playoff runs in recent seasons. [Guide](https://www.rugbycampus.org/learn/best-rugby-colleges-usa)
- **CRAA D1A vs NCR D1.** Two separate governing bodies run the top of men's college rugby. CRAA D1A plays its 15s national championship in the spring; NCR D1 plays its 15s championship in the fall. The very top of D1A is generally stronger than the top of NCR D1; the middle of both overlaps. A program can compete under one or both (UCLA plays both in 2026–27). [Guide](https://www.rugbycampus.org/learn/how-to-play-rugby-college-usa)
- **Varsity vs club.** Men's rugby is not an NCAA sport anywhere. Some programs are varsity (under the athletics department), others are clubs. Varsity status affects facilities, staff, funding and aid, and it can change, so check it is current. [Guide](https://www.rugbycampus.org/learn/when-college-rugby-programs-die)
- **Recruitment timeline.** There is no NCAA recruiting calendar for men's rugby. Send the first email to coaches eighteen months to two years before starting (the fall of junior year for US players), with a short note, a highlight reel, position, height and weight. Follow up once. Many US application deadlines fall between November and January; US college starts in August. Avoid the weeks around a coach's playoffs. [Guide](https://www.rugbycampus.org/learn/how-college-rugby-recruitment-works)
- **Scholarships.** Rugby scholarships exist but are rare, and every school does it differently. Athletic aid, where it exists, is most likely at varsity programs; many players get help through academic aid instead. Rugby Campus does not publish who pays what: ask the coach, compare the full cost to attend, and get any offer in writing. [Guide](https://www.rugbycampus.org/learn/rugby-scholarships-explained)
- **Getting seen.** Players do not need to be scouted. A short email with film is enough to get a look. Agencies are optional; using one alongside this site is fine. [Guide](https://www.rugbycampus.org/learn/how-college-rugby-recruitment-works)
